routes.reason: The new roadmap LogarithmicPotentialTheoryAndAlgebraicIntegers, 38 items, area algebraicnt, id free. I reproduced every negative search the route's reason claims, against the atlas at this commit: 'capacity', 'equilibrium measure', 'logarithmic potential', 'transfinite diameter', 'trace problem', 'Smyth' and 'totally positive algebraic integer' each return zero stages; 'potential theory' returns exactly one, the Tau Ceti PDE roadmap's lane on maximum principles and harmonic functions, which is a different subject with different objects; and the ten 'Chebyshev' hits are Chebyshev's ψ and θ functions in AnalyticNumberTheory AN.2 and the orthogonal-basis roadmap, not the extremal polynomials of a compact set whose norms compute the capacity. The rejection of a source route to ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.6 is right: CA.6 is 'Special algebraic numbers and Mahler measure' — house, Pisot and Salem classes — the neighbouring family, whereas the bulk of this paper is analysis (weighted potential theory, equilibrium measures, Chebyshev asymptotics, coefficient adjustment). A Part II was impossible because no roadmap has this direction to extend. The brief states the three final theorems exactly — Theorem 1.5 with its capacity > 1 and countably-many-components hypotheses, Theorem 5.11 that Smyth's method is optimal, and Theorem 1.1's λ_SSS < 1.89831 — and lays out the layers in the order the paper builds them. I would build it.

GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.1, 2 items. GN.1 is 'Convex-body and successive-minima theorems' and plans Blichfeldt and both Minkowski theorems, which is exactly what the items are; the paper uses them as inputs to the coefficient-adjustment construction.

ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.3 and CA.6, 4 items. CA.3 owns resultants and polynomial arithmetic; CA.6 owns special algebraic numbers, and routing the classical statement of the trace problem and λ_SSS there — rather than defining them inside the new roadmap — is what keeps the new roadmap importing the constant instead of defining it twice.

FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems R28.4, 4 items. The Honda–Tate input and the abelian-variety side of Corollary 1.3 belong with that roadmap; the Weil bound itself is separately marked planned at R34.1/R34.2 and DWP.1, which is the right split.
